thread:
sam: heads-up: onboarding verdant-9b (upstream release). license file calls itself 'Research Use Only (RUO) v1.0' and has a clause about service access. we planned INT8 for Dedicated perf testing. can we proceed?
julia: quick bench results from kevin: int8 latency down ~20%, throughput +25%, small eval hit on our safety test (false positive rate +0.6%). details: `evals/safety/verdant/int8/summary.json`
kevin: command used: `./bench --model verdant-9b --quant int8 --batch 8 --seq 1024`
sam: pasted license snippet below: 
"Research Use Only (RUO) v1.0
Licensed for non-commercial research and evaluation. Redistribution, sublicensing, and providing the Model via network services or API endpoints is prohibited without express written permission from the copyright holder."
anna (legal): that language is quite clear: "providing the Model via network services or API endpoints is prohibited". so public hosting or Dedicated access where customers call our endpoint would violate it.
anna (legal): options: 1) request hosting/commercial permission from upstream; 2) keep model strictly internal for research (gated infra, no external access); 3) ask customers to license directly and we provide integration (complex).
legal-bot: Ticket created LIC-3031 assigned to anna for upstream clarification.
model-registry-bot: registry note: verdant-9b status=RESEARCH_ONLY ticket=LIC-3031 updated_by=sam
julia: for transparency i'll attach the int8 artifact and eval diffs to the onboarding PR but mark as research-only. kevin, please ensure no public routes are enabled in the k8s manifest.
kevin: confirmed: test deployment is in the research namespace with network policies blocking external traffic.
sam: action items agreed: stop any customer-facing rollout, tag model as RESEARCH_ONLY in catalog/UI, legal to pursue LIC-3031 and ask about quantized derivatives exception.
anna (legal): small nuance to ask upstream: some licensors allow distributing quantized weights for non-commercial redistribution but still forbid hosting. i'll include a question about a quantized-derivative exception in LIC-3031.
julia: if we get written permission for hosting, int8 artifacts are reproducible and we can include them in a hosted bundle that meets perf targets. until then, internal-only.
sam: thanks all, pulling down any public routes now :thumbsup:
